messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content:
Lion (*Panthera leo*) belongs to the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebra (*Equus quagga*) belongs to the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  
Both of these orders are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which also contains orders such as Cetartiodactyla (whales, hippos, deer, pigs), Chiroptera (bats), and others.

Therefore, the most recent common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria.  
This ancestor lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleocene, before the diversification of the major Laurasiatherian lineages.
